preamble: ## Native libraries compiled into the Fetchpath binary
`fetchpath-core` depends on `curl = { features = ["static-curl", "http2"] }`, so
these C libraries are statically linked and are redistributed inside our
executable. Their versions come from the `-sys` crate versions in `Cargo.lock`,
and the licenses below were read from the upstream projects by a maintainer.
| Library | Version | Evidence | License |
| libcurl | 8.21.0 | `curl-sys 0.4.90+curl-8.21.0` in `Cargo.lock`, `static-curl` feature | curl license (MIT/X derivative), (c) Daniel Stenberg and many contributors |
| nghttp2 | 1.68.1 | `libnghttp2-sys 0.1.13+1.68.1` in `Cargo.lock`, `http2` feature | MIT, (c) Tatsuhiro Tsujikawa and nghttp2 contributors |
| zlib | inflate 1.3.2 | `libz-sys 1.1.29` in `Cargo.lock`; the built binary contains `inflate 1.3.2 Copyright 1995-2026 Mark Adler` | zlib license, (c) Jean-loup Gailly and Mark Adler |
TLS is **Schannel**, the TLS stack Windows itself provides. It is not
redistributed by us. The evidence is direct: `fetchpath-browser-host.exe`, which
links `fetchpath-core` and libcurl but no webview, contains 91 distinct
`schannel:` diagnostic strings from libcurl's Schannel backend and no OpenSSL
runtime symbols or version banner. `openssl-src`, the crate that would vendor and
compile OpenSSL, does not appear in `Cargo.lock` at all; `openssl-sys` and
`openssl-probe` are present in the graph only as platform-gated dependencies of
`curl` and are not linked into a Windows build.
## Runtime components Fetchpath does not redistribute
- **Microsoft Edge WebView2 Runtime.** Supplied and serviced by Microsoft. The
installer is configured with `webviewInstallMode: downloadBootstrapper`, so it
downloads Microsoft's bootstrapper when the runtime is missing rather than
carrying a copy.
- **yt-dlp and ffmpeg.** Needed only for saving video and audio, and never
bundled. A user who wants them chooses to fetch them from their publishers
through Settings, or points Fetchpath at a copy they already have. The
versions, download locations, publisher checksum sources and licenses are in
`adapters/media/media-tools.json`, and the license of each is shown
in the application before anything is downloaded. ffmpeg builds are
distributed under the GPL; because Fetchpath neither ships nor links them,
that license applies to the user's own copy rather than to Fetchpath.
appendix: node tools/licenses/generate.mjs --check  # fail if it is out of date
The `--check` form runs with the rest of the repository checks, so a new
dependency cannot reach a release without appearing here.
